cards.front: Recall a key point about Adjective Endings and Pronouns
cards.back: Grammar accuracy is essential for the writing and speaking papers, where it is worth up to 40% of marks. Always check cases, word order and verb endings.

cards.front: What should you know about german exam tips — adjective endings and pronouns?
cards.back: 1. For Adjective Endings and Pronouns, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Adjective Endings and Pronouns, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
adjective ending (e.g. Die Adjektivendung hängt vom Fall ab.)
strong / weak (declension) (e.g. Nach 'der' ist die Endung schwach.)
predicate (after sein) (e.g. Prädikative Adjektive haben keine Endung.)
attributive (before noun) (e.g. Attributive Adjektive brauchen Endungen.)
personal pronoun (e.g. 'Ihn' ist das Personalpronomen im Akkusativ.)
relative pronoun (e.g. 'Der, die, das' sind Relativpronomen.)
relative clause (e.g. Im Relativsatz steht das Verb am Ende.)
to decline / inflect (e.g. Man muss Adjektive nach Fall und Gender beugen.)
referent pronoun (e.g. Das Relativpronomen bezieht sich auf das Nomen.)
vowel change (e.g. Manche Adjektive haben Umlaut im Komparativ.)
comparison (degrees) (e.g. Positiv, Komparativ, Superlativ sind die Steigerungsformen.)

Students often forget word order in subordinate clauses. Wrong: Weil ich krank bin, ich bleibe zu Hause. Correct: Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause (in the MAIN clause after a subordinate clause, the verb comes FIRST, then the subject).
